subject: Scalable commit matrix with fallthrough pricing and cushion allocator

Subject: RFP follow-up: commercial asks and burst handling

Markus — thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to get a clearer picture on how Redwood would price for both steady-state and burst traffic across our fleet of microservices. Two items they specifically asked us to clarify: 1) how committed monthly/annual token volumes map to per-token pricing and overage mechanics; and 2) what happens to latency-sensitive calls if our dedicated pool saturates (fallthrough behavior and cost delta).

Attached is the RFP commercial worksheet (we filled in projected consumption buckets). Can you provide a compact set of scenarios showing: committed tiers, per-token rates (for generation and embeddings), a burst cushion proposal that applies cross-services, and a fallthrough pricing example (i.e., hosted model substitute or queued requests with discounting/credits)?

Appreciate a short matrix we can bring to the sourcing committee on Friday.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Director, Platform Procurement
GreenGrid Systems

Lena — thanks for the clear asks and the worksheet. Pushing back a compact proposal and an example matrix for the committee. High level summary below; full scenario table attached as a spreadsheet and a short term-sheet PDF.

Summary (draft):
- Commit structure: monthly token commit with optional annual prepay. We propose three bands for GreenGrid: 200M, 600M, and 1.6B tokens/month (all-token aggregate across gen+embed).
- Baseline rates (committed): $0.00060 per 1k tokens (200M), $0.00050 per 1k tokens (600M), $0.00042 per 1k tokens (1.6B) — applies to both generation and embeddings for contracted models.
- Overages: over-commit tokens billed monthly at a blended overage rate of committed_tier_rate * 1.5 (for predictable budgeting). Example: 200M tier overage = $0.00090/1k.
- Cushion allocator (burst pool): we recommend a shared monthly cushion equal to 10% of the committed volume (non-cumulative, resets each month). Tokens consumed from cushion are billed at committed_tier_rate and do not count as overage; cushion protects against short spikes and is pooled across services.
- Fallthrough/fallback behavior: if dedicated capacity can’t satisfy low-latency requests, traffic falls through to Redwood hosted endpoints or to a lower-cost model variant. Fallthrough pricing = hosted list rate for the chosen model variant, plus a failover surcharge that we discount by 20% as a contractual credit (net effective delta ~ +25–40% vs committed rate depending on tier). We explicitly include SLA-triggered credits if fallthrough exceeds the monthly threshold.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups by default; annual true-up option available with prepay discounts.

I attached: pricing-scenarios-v3.xlsx (scenarios matrix), fallthrough-term-sheet-draft.pdf (one-page summary). We thought to include two commercially distinct paths: commit-first (lower unit price + smaller cushion) or cushion-first (larger cushion, slightly higher baseline unit price).

Next steps: would you like a one-pager that maps your worksheet buckets to our three preferred commit bands, or shall we schedule a 30m call with procurement this week to walk the committee through the matrix?

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-pricing-scenarios-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Procurement — answers below with a worked example and the policy text you can pass to Legal.

1) Worked invoice example (600M tier):
   - Committed volume: 600,000,000 tokens/month at $0.00050 per 1k = $300.00 per 1M tokens -> monthly committed charge = $300,000.
   - Monthly cushion: 10% of commit = 60,000,000 tokens billed at committed rate if used (no overage). If your one-week spike consumes 250M additional tokens, consumption layout: 60M cushion + 190M overage.
   - Overage calculation: 190,000,000 tokens billed at overage rate $0.00075 per 1k (note: we apply 1.5x to the committed per-1k rate expressed in our spreadsheet as a blended overage multiplier) -> overage charge = $142,500.
   - Total month invoice = committed $300,000 + cushion $0 (billed at committed rate only if used; if used, it's part of usage not a separate line) + overage $142,500 = $442,500.

2) Capacity-hedge for Hosted fallthrough (48-hour failover):
   - If Dedicated capacity is unavailable and traffic routes to Hosted for <=72 hours, we apply a capacity-hedge credit equal to 50% of the delta between hosted list rate and committed rate for the tokens processed during the failover window. That credit posts automatically as an invoice-level line item on next bill.
   - Example: hosted list rate for the equivalent model = $0.00095/1k; delta vs committed ($0.00050/1k) = $0.00045/1k. For 48 hours of 10M tokens: raw delta = $4,500; capacity-hedge credit = 50% * $4,500 = $2,250 credited to the invoice.

3) Step-down / reduction mechanics:
   - Mid-term reductions: allowed at quarterly true-up points with a 60-day notice. Reductions above 30% from prior committed band trigger a step-down fee equal to 10% of the annualized difference between prior and new commit for the remaining term, unless GreenGrid elects an annual true-up and prepay option which permits one step-down per 12mo without fee.

Other commercial notes:
- Multi-year discount: additional 8% on baseline unit price for 2-year agreements with annual true-up and 12% for 3-year prepay.
- Payment terms: Net 45 standard; Net 30 available at sign with a 0.75% price uplift if required.
- SLA credits: uptime SLOs baked into term sheet; sustained fallthrough >6% of monthly requests triggers escalating credits.

Attached are a short worked example page and the draft fallthrough clause for your counsel. Happy to hop on a 30m session with legal if that helps expedite.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Commercial Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: fallthrough-term-sheet-draft.pdf (document)]
